rules.rule: A string replace that does not match FAILS SILENTLY and leaves the file half-edited. Never patch a file with an unverified `s.replace(...)` and move on. Either use an ANCHORED edit that errors when the anchor is missing, or assert the change landed before continuing — `assert new in s`, or re-read the file. AND THE WORSE SIBLING: an escape that survives the heredoc as a CONTROL CHARACTER. Writing a regex through a heredoc turned every intended \b into a literal U+0008 backspace inside a RAW string, so the pattern compiled cleanly and matched nothing anywhere.
rules.why: s097, FOUR times in one session. A call site was left pointing at a renamed function; a print block kept referencing a field that no longer existed; a signature changed on one side only; and the run-recording block never entered the cycle at all — I only noticed because the state file did not appear. The common cause is a non-ASCII character in the match text: the middle dot in 'ran · failed' did not match through a heredoc, so the replace returned the string unchanged and the script reported success. THE SCRIPT SAID IT WORKED. Each of these cost a full re-run, and one shipped a broken file to a background job that then failed on its own. || s097, the same root with a different symptom and it cost far more: _numbers_in_prose() returned 0 across 3,544 long-string leaves in 92 stores. I retyped the 'identical' line outside the module, it worked, and I concluded the bug was scope or shadowing — because retyping produced a real two-character escape while the file held control bytes. I marked the checker BROKEN and moved on. The actual fix was one line. THE TELL: when a regex matches NOTHING ANYWHERE, doubt the PATTERN BYTES before the logic — `git diff | cat -A` shows them, reasoning does not.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. anchored edits by preference — a missing anchor must ERROR, not no-op. 2. if you must use replace, ASSERT the result changed: `assert s != before` per hunk, not once at the end. 3. never put non-ASCII in a match string; anchor on ASCII-only lines. 4. after patching, RUN the thing — syntax-checking is not enough, a silent no-op parses perfectly. 5. patching the same file in several fragments compounds this: read it whole first. 6. never write a regex or an escape-bearing literal through a heredoc — use the editor. 7. a pattern matching nothing anywhere is a corrupted literal until proven otherwise: hexdump it. 8. when you write a docstring ABOUT an escape, remember the docstring is not raw either.

rules.rule: The bootstrap index is GENERATED from the stores, never written — and it must carry the SHAPE of the installation, not only its inventory: the process spine ranked by domains served, the cross-cutting topics that are NOT domains, and the measured maturity. One read must give the PROFILE, including what CANNOT be seen.
rules.why: s097. The index listed modules, layers and counts — an inventory — and a session could read all of it and still not know that this tenant exists to run BUDGET-TO-REPORT, that SECURITY is a column and not a domain so searching for it returns nothing, or that 80% of traffic is external so any answer assuming people in screens is wrong before it starts. That is SHAPE, and shape is what makes an inventory usable. Ranking B2R first because SIX domains serve it — measured, not asserted — also means the order corrects itself if the installation changes.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. every block DERIVED from a store; if it cannot be derived it does not belong in the index. 2. rank by measurement, never by opinion. 3. name what CANNOT be seen — a session that does not know the blind spot reads absence as evidence. 4. cross-cutting topics get their own section precisely BECAUSE they are not domains: if the only way to find security is to already know it is column E, the index has failed.
rules.evidence: brain_v2/build_brain_index.py: _process_spine, _security_block, _integration_block, _maturity_block; index 4.0KB -> 9.6KB, all generated

rules.rule: A capability column that is asked N times and OWNED BY NOBODY stays empty in every row. When a column is systemically empty, the first hypothesis is NOT neglect — it is that the topic has no SUBJECT: no store, no composer, no place where the answer accumulates. Give it a cross-cutting subject and the column fills; keep treating it as N independent gaps and it never will.
rules.why: s097, TWO instances in one session and they behave identically. E_AUTH was empty in 16 of 21 domains and searching the domain list for 'security' returned nothing — it was a column with no subject. R_S4_READINESS was empty in 21 of 21, the only COMPLETELY empty column, and it had a sub-scorecard nobody owned. Both filled the moment they got a store, a composer and a section in the bootstrap index. The corollary bites too: because the S/4 sub-scorecard held only SIX TECHNICAL factors, a COMMERCIAL exposure (digital access / API cost — arguably the largest for an 80%-external tenant) had nowhere to land and simply was not recorded. A subject shapes what can be seen, so an incomplete subject is a blind spot with a structure.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. a systemically empty column => ask WHO OWNS IT before asking who neglected it. 2. build the subject as a store composed of components, each saying what it needs and whether we hold it — never an empty section, because an empty security or readiness report reads as GOOD NEWS. 3. give it a section in the bootstrap index: if the only way to find a topic is to already know which column it is, the index has failed. 4. check the subject's own factor list for a MISSING KIND — technical factors only usually means a commercial or organisational dimension is invisible.
rules.evidence: brain_v2/build_security_posture.py (E_AUTH) and brain_v2/build_s4_readiness.py (R_S4_READINESS, 21 of 21 empty, 6 technical factors + 1 commercial added); claims #404 #406 #407

rules.rule: Measure the system against WHAT IT DOES TODAY, not against what a design document once specified. A design doc is archaeology and vocabulary; it is not a conformance target unless someone still intends it. Before treating any as-designed statement as a yardstick, ASK WHETHER IT WAS SUPERSEDED — and go looking for the current-state research FIRST, because it is usually harder to find than the blueprints and always worth more.
rules.why: s097. I ingested five 2017 blueprints and produced 17 conformance rules whose verdicts were mostly NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Every measurement was real. The FRAME was wrong: UNESCO kept SAP as the system of RECORD and deliberately moved the system of ENGAGEMENT outside it, so 'the blueprint specified X and X does not exist' describes a design that became irrelevant, not a system that failed. The peer project's own current-state research had ALREADY NAMED this failure mode — it re-scored one of its claims as 'a DESIGN-DOC ARTIFACT OVERTAKEN BY THE AS-RUN' and deprecated any dialog-based baseline with 'a redesign baselined on dialog usage is baselined on <20% of the real traffic'. I walked into the trap their document describes, because sources/2017_design/ was easier to find than knowledge/36 and knowledge/37.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. look for the AS-RUN research before the design corpus — filenames like 'asrun', 'e2e', 'current', 'operating model' beat 'BBP' and 'design'. 2. when a design statement fails against data, the FIRST hypothesis is that it was superseded, not that the system is broken. 3. a NOT_IMPLEMENTED verdict needs a second question: does anyone still intend it? If not, it is history. 4. keep what a blueprint is genuinely good for — VOCABULARY. The AVC address triple named a distinction we had measured and had no word for, and that survives the reframe. 5. the real yardstick is the measured end-to-end: here, human validation at ~21 days against an integration seam of 1.8 days says the leverage is human throughput, which no blueprint comparison would have shown.
rules.evidence: claim superseding the framing of #409/410/414/415; unesco-sap-brain/knowledge/36_asrun_operating_model_reeval.md and 37_workplan_e2e_integrated.md

rules.rule: When a join/lookup between two tables returns nothing, compare the FIELD WIDTHS of the two key columns (DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET) before extracting any more tables chasing the link. A join between two differently-sized keys sharing the same field NAME cannot ever succeed, no matter how many more tables are pulled.
rules.why: s098, A16_payroll_end_to_end. Three separate extractions chased the payroll symbolic-account-to-GL-account link through T030/T030B/T52EZ before a single DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET call ended the line of enquiry: T030-KTOSL (the FI account-determination transaction key) is CHAR(3); a payroll symbolic account (T52EK-SYMKO) is CHAR(4). Two different keys wearing the same field name — no join could ever have worked. The cost was three extractions instead of one field-metadata call.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. The moment a join/lookup against a candidate key returns zero or nonsensical results, STOP extracting more candidate tables. 2. Call DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET (or read the DDIC) on BOTH sides of the join and compare LENG. 3. If the widths differ, the fields are NOT the same key regardless of the shared name — go find the real bridge (often a customer-range table, see feedback about T9POST) or read the POSTED DOCUMENTS instead of the configuration (companion rule). 4. Record the field-width fact in algorithm_memory so no other algorithm repeats the same trap.
rules.evidence: brain_v2/methods/algorithm_memory.json subject '_field_width'; claims #463/#464; brain_v2/payroll_discovery.json .resolved_posting._why_config_search_fails

rules.rule: When the configuration tables will not yield an assignment (a derivation, an account determination, a routing decision), read the POSTED DOCUMENTS instead — the resolved result sits on one row there, and the cardinality measured IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (forward and back) identifies where the decision is actually made.
rules.why: s098, A16_payroll_end_to_end part 7 ('the resolved posting'). The payroll account determination defeated a configuration search for a structural reason (see feedback_compare_field_widths_before_more_extraction). PPDIT — the posting document ITEMS — carries the FI transaction key and the resolved GL account together on one row. Over a 4,000-row sample: 2 of 4 keys fan out to several GL accounts, while 28 of 28 GL accounts belong to exactly one key. One-to-many forward, one-to-one back — which is what proved the account is decided BEYOND the key (by the wage type), a reading no configuration table could have given directly.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. If a customizing/derivation table search stalls (empty joins, structurally mismatched keys, or the mechanism is simply not configured where standard SAP would put it), pivot to the TRANSACTIONAL documents that the process actually produced. 2. Read a representative sample keyed the same way the decision is made (same company code / same period) and pull BOTH the input key and the resolved output field on the same row. 3. Compute cardinality BOTH ways (key→outputs and output→keys) — the direction that collapses to 1 is where the decision is actually made. 4. This is faster AND more truthful than reconstructing configuration: it does not depend on having found the right customizing table at all.
rules.evidence: brain_v2/methods/algorithm_memory.json subject '_read_the_documents_not_the_configuration'; brain_v2/methods/algorithms.json A16_payroll_end_to_end.seventh_part_added_s098; claims #463/#464

rules.rule: Read the transport TEXT (E07T) before drawing a conclusion from a transport VOLUME trend. A trend measured on object/row counts alone invites a reading the content refutes.
rules.why: s098, A17_change_governance / AN-TRANSPORTED-DATA-LEGITIMACY. Transported table (TABU) content rose roughly tenfold from August to November 2025 on an unchanged transport cadence — read on volume alone, this looks like an intervention in production master data. E07T (the transport texts, previously never extracted — cts_transports was built without as4text) showed the volume was overwhelmingly holiday calendars (137 objects across 12 transports) and HR form scenarios (492 objects): legitimate, routine content, not a data-move incident. The volume-only reading would have escalated a non-issue.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. Before characterizing ANY transport-volume trend (a spike, a rise, an unusual cadence) as suspicious or as evidence of an intervention, pull E07T (or the transport's AS4TEXT) for the objects/transports driving it. 2. Read what the transport SAYS it is for, not just how much it moved. 3. Only escalate a volume trend once the text has been read and does NOT explain it. 4. This generalizes the companion lesson about reading posted documents over configuration: read what was RECORDED about the change (the text), not just what was counted (the volume).
rules.evidence: brain_v2/methods/algorithm_memory.json subject 'transported content' (second entry, 's098', 'the transport TEXT reversed the reading the volume trend suggested'); brain_v2/capability_model/execution_backlog.json AN-TRANSPORTED-DATA-LEGITIMACY (DONE)

rules.rule: A COMPANION NAMES THE OBJECTS. It never reports a count in place of them. If the artefact holds 18 enhancements, the page lists the 18 — each with WHERE it hooks, WHAT FIELD it decides on, WHAT it modifies, and WHETHER THE EFFECT SURVIVES the call. Four structural requirements: (1) every quantity is immediately followed by its enumeration; (2) every object carries its hook, its gate and its effect, not just its name; (3) every figure carries the perimeter it was measured on, in the same cell; (4) the page states which sections are GENERATED from the brain and which are WRITTEN, because only the written ones can go stale.
rules.why: s098, USER on the first budget-rate companion: 'es muy generico, no dice las extensiones que hacen cuales son en que momento, no da ninguna informacion, el nivel de explicacion es pobre'. Correct, and measurable: the page said 'nine enhancements and a control report' while budget_rate_enhancements.json held 18 members each with hook, gate_keyed_on, modifies and persists; 12 moments each with its SAP object, its gate and the DATE it converts on; and 8 named perimeter conditions. Every one of those was summarised away. A COUNT IS WHAT YOU WRITE WHEN YOU HAVE NOT READ THE DATA — and it is indistinguishable, to the reader, from having read it and found nothing. Rebuilt, the same page went from 33 KB of assertions to 45 KB in which a reader can find that ZFIX_EXCHANGERATE_CHECK_CONS hooks CL_FM_EF_POSITION->CHECK_CONSUMPTION, gates on the RESERVATION HEADER currency, and does NOT persist — it restores the value after the standard check.
rules.how_to_apply: Before publishing any companion, take each section and ask: could a reader ACT on this, or does it only tell them a thing exists? 'Nine enhancements' fails; 'ZFIX_EF_FUND_RESERVATION, on KBLP/KBLK during FMX1/FMX2, gating on the reservation header currency, writing hwges — PERSISTS' passes. Render the artefact's own arrays as TABLES rather than prose summaries: the detail is already structured, and summarising structured data into a sentence is a lossy transformation with no benefit. Where an array exists in the source, a table must exist in the page.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-002 says lossy compression only at query-time, never at storage-time — and a companion is a QUERY over the brain, not a store. But the compression it applies must be SELECTION (which objects matter here) and never AGGREGATION INTO A COUNT, because a count destroys precisely what a reader came for. CP-003 also binds: 'nine enhancements' is an approximation where an exact enumeration was available at zero cost.
rules.evidence: companions/budget_rate_companion_v1.html §14 (per-extension section, 15 enumerated); brain_v2/budget_rate_enhancements.json (18 members, 12 moments, 8 perimeter conditions)

rules.rule: When a subagent or a background write dies mid-stream, DIFF what it touched before doing anything else. It does not leave a broken file — it leaves a file that is VALID AND DIFFERENT, so parsing it, loading it and running a smoke test all pass.
rules.why: s098. The steward close pass died with 'API Error: Response stalled mid-stream'. It left feedback_rules.json parseable, loadable and wrong: domain_axes — the convention in 144 of 187 rules — replaced by a flat domain field, and the trailing newline dropped. Nothing would have caught it except reading the diff. The same shape of damage is why an interrupted post-INSERT DROP once left FMIOI duplicated and it looked like a clean load.
rules.how_to_apply: On any agent-failure notification: git status, then git diff on every file it named, BEFORE re-running it or committing. Judge each change against the file's OWN convention — count which shape the existing entries use rather than assuming. Keep what the agent got right: here the evidence field it added was useful and only the schema change was wrong. And do NOT re-run a writer that died mid-write until the partial state is resolved. The measured split in s098 was 144 domain_axes / 17 domain / 26 neither, so the majority settled which convention was correct — the file answered the question.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 is knowledge over velocity: re-running the failed agent is the fast path and it compounds damage over a state nobody inspected. Reading the diff costs one command and is the only thing that sees this class of defect.
rules.evidence: git diff brain_v2/agent_rules/feedback_rules.json after task a3be7b85e103b79e6 failed

rules.rule: Never publish a query, command or reproduction step you have not EXECUTED and seen return the figure you are printing beside it. A recipe you have not run is the same defect as a count you have not read: it looks like knowledge and is a guess — and it is worse, because the reader will trust it enough to act.
rules.why: s098, the 'how to reproduce every figure' section of the budget-rate companion. Nine queries were written, then all nine were run against the golden and each returned its published figure exactly (USD 1,982,154.59 / EUR 796,418.86; net 0.00 per currency; 2,316 runs and 488 posted; 72 configured and 0 posting; 14 fund types). Running them also surfaced what the queries needed to SAY: that ppdit no longer needs a run filter because it is already purged, and that the chain query multiplies because FI summarises several payroll items into one line.
rules.how_to_apply: Write the query, run it, paste the ACTUAL result beside it, and add the caveat that running it taught you. If it cannot be run — because it needs a live system or a table not held — say so in place of the figure rather than printing an expected one.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 demands verifiable evidence. A published query IS a claim about what the data will say, and an unexecuted one has no evidence behind it at all.
rules.evidence: companions/budget_rate_companion_v1.html §16 (9 recetas); scratchpad repro_test.py

rules.rule: Never judge whether a data field is alive from ONE measurement. Three axes, always together: (1) FILL, tested against the field's own TYPE — a numeric or NUMC column is never blank, it defaults to zero, so use trim(trim(col),'0.') and not a plain not-empty test; (2) TREND, grouped by the ROW's creation date — a flat low rate and a decaying one are opposite findings; (3) CARDINALITY — a field populated on 42% of rows carrying ONE distinct value has a fill rate and no information. A verdict is only trustworthy when all three agree.
rules.why: s098, algorithm A19 over PRPS's 31 custom fields. Each axis alone produced a WRONG answer, measured: a plain not-empty test called ten of the 31 fully populated when YYE_PRCTO is 0.45% real (60,021 of its 60,292 values are '0.00'); YYE_DONOR reads as never-adopted at 18.5% flat and is a twenty-four-year abandonment curve from 82% to 5% once grouped by creation year; and YYE_IMPL_AGENCY is filled on 42% of elements with exactly ONE distinct value, which no fill rate can ever detect. Running all three also found what one axis had hidden — THREE fields abandoning on the same curve, not one, and one field (YYE_APPR_LINE) being ADOPTED that had been read as residual.
rules.how_to_apply: Use A19 (process_mining/wbs_model.py) or replicate its three measurements. If a field has no trend data, report SIN DATOS rather than guessing from the other two. And when reporting, give the reader all three numbers — a verdict without its axes cannot be challenged.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 requires maximum precision and checkable facts. A single-axis verdict is an approximation presented as a finding, and this rule exists because that approximation was wrong three different ways on the same table.
rules.evidence: brain_v2/project_wbs_model.json (A19); companions/project_wbs_companion_v1.html

rules.rule: A substring match is NOT evidence that a fact is already stored. Before concluding that knowledge is persisted, READ THE RECORD the keyword hit — the same word routinely appears in an unrelated rule. A coverage check that only reports yes/no is a coverage check that will lie to you.
rules.why: s098, twice in one session and in mirror-image forms. First: checking for an existing rule by EXACT ID missed feedback_a_dead_agent_leaves_a_valid_different_file and a duplicate was written. Then, over-correcting, a concept search reported the three-axis method and the authorship lesson as ALREADY PRESENT — 'cardinality' had hit a rule about ROWSKIPS rejection and 'authorship' had hit feedback_only_modify_our_own_code. Both were false positives and both would have left real knowledge in the chat. One failure mode says 'not there' when it is; the other says 'there' when it is not, and the second is worse because it ends the search.
rules.how_to_apply: Print the id and the first line of every record the probe matched, and judge them by eye. Two lines of output turn a boolean into evidence. Do this before writing a new record AND before deciding not to.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 puts traceability above velocity: a false 'already covered' loses the knowledge silently and nobody ever learns to look for it, which is the irreversible kind of loss.
rules.evidence: scratchpad gap2.py reported SI for both; gap3.py printing the matched records showed neither existed

rules.rule: A rule that can only be obeyed by REMEMBERING it will be broken, including by the agent that wrote it. For any failure that is MECHANICAL — a substitution that must land, an output that must match its generator, a store that must be searched before writing — do not add a rule. Add a CHECK that runs and fails loudly. If the check cannot be written, say so explicitly instead of writing a rule that will read as coverage and provide none.
rules.why: s098, and the evidence is against myself. Rule #180 — 'a silent replace is a silent defect' — ALREADY EXISTED and I broke it FOUR times in this one session: each time a template replace missed its anchor, the script printed OK because the Python still parsed, and the page shipped with a raw token or a stray %s. Every one was caught afterwards, by hand, one at a time. Three companions carried the line 'never edit the HTML, edit the builder' and nothing verified it — when a check was finally written, its FIRST run found budget_rate_graph.json already out of step with its generator, and nobody had known. The dedup discipline failed twice more, in mirror-image forms. Four documented rule-violations by the author of the rules is not a discipline problem; it is proof that rules do not work on mechanical failures.
rules.how_to_apply: When about to write a feedback rule, ask first: could a script detect this violation? If yes, write the script and let the rule point at it. The rules store is for JUDGEMENT — what to measure, what to distrust, when to stop. Mechanical invariants belong in scripts/verify_generated.py, brain_v2/promote.py, brain_v2/verify_claims.py and their siblings, and the close should RUN them rather than recite them.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 puts traceability above velocity. A rule nobody can execute produces the APPEARANCE of a control while the loss keeps happening silently, which is the irreversible failure it warns against — the loss is invisible precisely because a rule exists.
rules.evidence: scripts/verify_generated.py first run found budget_rate_graph.json drifted; rule #180 existed and was violated 4x in s098; dedup failed 2x

rules.rule: Any automated check that reports CANDIDATES rather than certainties must be able to record 'reviewed and deliberately excluded', with the reason written beside it. Without that, it repeats the same finding every run, the reader learns to skip it, and the control silently becomes decoration — while still appearing to be a control, which is worse than having none. A gate with no memory of its own decisions can only repeat itself.
rules.why: s098, on the first real use of stop_integrity_hook.py. It flagged ten process_mining scripts as absent from the algorithm arsenal. Triaged one by one, EIGHT are helpers or pipeline steps of 54-135 lines, two are analyses, none declares itself an algorithm and none is reusable on another installation — which is the bar. The honest verdict was that NONE should be registered. But that verdict had nowhere to live, so the gate would have reported the same ten every session forever. The degradation the hook was explicitly designed to avoid reappeared through the back door, one commit after the design note warning about it.
rules.how_to_apply: Give the check an explicit exclusion set IN THE CODE, with a comment saying when it was triaged and on what basis — never a silent filter. Then verify BOTH directions: that it goes quiet on the reviewed set, and that it still fires on a newly introduced case. The second test is the one that proves the exclusion did not just switch the check off.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 values traceability: an exclusion with its reason recorded is traceable, while a check quietly ignored by its reader loses the signal AND the record that a decision was ever made.
rules.evidence: brain_v2/stop_integrity_hook.py NOT_ALGORITHMS; verified quiet on the ten and firing on a new file

rules.rule: A backup that has never been RESTORED is a hypothesis. Every backup this project writes must ship with a rehearsed restore, and the recovery runbook must live in the REPO so it can be read from origin when the machine it describes is gone. Six rules: MEASURE before designing (the irreplaceable asset is rarely the big one); EXCLUDE with the reason written down; VERIFY the exclusion by reading the written package, not by trusting the filter; REFUSE to write an empty backup; RESTORE to a staging directory, never over the live target; and state explicitly what is NOT recoverable.
rules.why: s098. Every session close for months had RESTATED that the Golden DB and ~/.claude are local-only and git does not protect them. When it was finally checked there were ZERO copies of either and no script to make one — stating a risk is not managing it, and a reminder that repeats and is never executed is the APPEARANCE of a control, which is worse than none because nobody looks again. The same session also had 73 unpushed commits: git protects nothing you have not pushed. And measuring inverted the intuition — 1,836 MB of transcripts and 16.33 GB of database are both reconstructible, while the 1.5 MB of memory is the only thing nothing can rebuild. Then TESTING the backup found it captured 4 files and zero memory (pathlib resolves `dir/**` as directories, not recursive files) AND wrote the package anyway.
rules.how_to_apply: Follow the universal standard at ecosystem-coordinator/.knowledge/way-of-working/project-durability-and-recovery.md. Reference implementation: scripts/backup_golden.py (both assets, one --dest) and knowledge/recovery_runbook.md. Rehearse with `--restore <pkg> --to <tmp>` and paste the ACTUAL output into the runbook — the last real drill, not the expected one. And bound the worst case for reconstructible assets with a manifest of what was loaded and under which rules; without it recovery is archaeology, with it it is a script.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 puts traceability above velocity and calls losing it irreversible. Losing the memory of WHY a decision was made is the purest form of that loss, and it is the asset with the least protection precisely because it is the smallest.
rules.evidence: knowledge/recovery_runbook.md; drill 595 files in / 595 out / 474 memory, OK; scripts/backup_golden.py aborts below 50 memory files

rules.rule: Triage every support item into one of TWO tracks BEFORE any lookup or analysis. TRACK A = DIAGNOSIS: the unknown is why the system behaved this way; the output is a root cause. TRACK B = OPERATIONAL ACTION: what to do is already known and executing it correctly is the work; the output is an executed, verified change plus the reusable procedure. Tell them apart in one read: an action verb aimed at a named person/entity from someone with the authority to ask for it is B; a symptom, an error number, a 'this fails' is A. Ambiguous items default to A unless there is an authorizing document, in which case they are B.
rules.why: s099. The skill had one protocol shaped entirely around diagnosis, so the operational changes (INC-000006313, INC-000011781) were pushed through a root-cause workflow that asks the wrong questions. Track B's risks are not Track A's: A fails by chasing the wrong mechanism (INC-000005240 burned 154K tokens on FMDERIVE), B fails by executing the requester's summary instead of the authority and by never looking at the population around the change. One protocol for both means one set of blind spots applied to work that does not share them.
rules.how_to_apply: Step 0 of .agents/skills/sap_incident_analyst/SKILL.md. State the track explicitly in your first response on the ticket, and say why. If you find yourself writing 'how it should work' for a request that is just 'add this person', you triaged wrong. Both tracks still share: BRAIN LOOKUP, provisional-until-confirmed, the user gate, and rebuild-only-at-the-end.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 demands precision anchored in evidence. Naming the kind of work before doing it is the first precision available; skipping it makes every later step approximate.
rules.evidence: .agents/skills/sap_incident_analyst/SKILL.md Step 0; INC-000006313 + INC-000011781 vs INC-000005240

rules.rule: On any operational change, the authorizing DOCUMENT is the specification — never the requester's summary. Read the TRS letter, the bank carton, the signed approval, and execute the full set of operations it mandates, including the ones nobody mentioned. No authority document = no change spec; stop and ask.
rules.why: INC-000011781. The request said 'can you please add Renata RITTER for UBO in BCM'. The two authoritative TRS letters (FIN.8/MOD/10.0000003618 and ...3617, both 24/03/2026) said ADD Ritter AND DELETE Von Michael MARTIN. Executing the note would have added the new signatory and left an unauthorized one active on two bank accounts. A requester's note is a pointer to the change, not the change.
rules.how_to_apply: Track B step B1. Record the authority reference, its date, its effective date, and the complete operation list. Use the authority's effective date as BEGDA, not the execution date — INC-000006313 used the execution date and opened a 7-day audit gap for nothing.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 requires verifiable evidence behind every action. A forwarded sentence is not evidence of what was authorized; the signed letter is.
rules.evidence: knowledge/incidents/INC-000011781_ubo_bcm_add_ritter.md §1-§4; INC-000006313 BEGDA gap

rules.rule: After executing an operational change, reconcile the ENTIRE population against the authority — not just the row you touched. Whatever the sweep finds becomes a recurring check under Zagentexecution/quality_checks/. This is Track B's equivalent of Track A's class generalization: one ticket, one standing control.
rules.why: INC-000011781. Nobody asked us to audit the UBO panel; the ask was to add one person. The sweep against the carton found De Sousa Carvalho 10016038 active on all 4 nodes with full signing rights and BCM_REV_REJ_PAY since Jan-2024 while absent from the carton — roughly 18 months of over-authorization that no standing control was looking for. The ticket was not the finding; the ticket was the occasion to look.
rules.how_to_apply: Track B step B8. Diff the system population against the authority document, both directions (present-but-unauthorized AND authorized-but-missing). Promote the diff to a script. The BCM family is the worked pattern: bcm_signatory_reconciliation_check.py, bcm_role_gap_check.py, bcm_release_vs_approve.py.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 puts knowledge above velocity. Closing the ticket at the row you changed is the fast path; sweeping the population is where the ticket turns into knowledge that outlives it.
rules.evidence: knowledge/incidents/INC-000011781_ubo_bcm_add_ritter.md §0; Zagentexecution/quality_checks/bcm_*.py

rules.rule: Track the occurrence count of every operational scenario. 1st occurrence leaves an incident doc + a first-class record + the rules doc that explains target selection. 2nd occurrence MUST leave a procedure doc + a recurring check + a companion, so the 3rd is mechanical. From the 3rd on, execute from the procedure; if you had to re-derive anything, the procedure was incomplete and fixing it is part of that ticket.
rules.why: s099. This is how the ecosystem gets cheaper instead of merely busier. The BCM signatory pattern proves it: the 2nd execution (INC-000011781) was faster than the 1st (INC-000006313) AND caught drift the 1st never looked for, because the 1st had left behind bcm_signatory_rules.md and a reconciliation check. Without that promotion step, each ticket re-derives the same mechanism and the cost per ticket stays flat forever.
rules.how_to_apply: Track B step B9. Before closing, ask: how many times have we done this scenario? Look it up via the incident records' `scenario` field. If the answer is >=2 and there is no procedure doc, writing it is part of the ticket, not a nice-to-have.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001: velocity that leaves no trace is the expensive kind. A procedure written on the 2nd occurrence is traceability that pays compound interest.
rules.evidence: INC-000006313 -> INC-000011781; knowledge/domains/Treasury/bcm_signatory_change_solution_design.md

rules.rule: An incident is not captured until it has a first-class record in brain_v2/incidents/incidents.json. A markdown file under knowledge/incidents/ is prose on disk: BRAIN LOOKUP traverses brain_state.incidents -> indexes.by_incident -> objects[X], and a doc with no record is in none of those. Gate it with Zagentexecution/quality_checks/incident_record_coverage_check.py.
rules.why: s099 opened and found 11 docs on disk against 7 records. Three incidents were invisible: INC-000011781 (the richest BCM signatory precedent we have — IT1218 node selection, the drift sweep, the role gap), INC-180995 and INC-CLASS-LOSS-2026-06. The PMO had recorded 'TODO: run rebuild_all.py to fold INC-000011781 in' on 2026-06-18 and it never ran. A TODO is not a control; the next agent on a sibling BCM ticket would have started from zero.
rules.how_to_apply: Write the record in the SAME action as the doc, never 'later'. Before closing any support work run the check (exit 0 = clean) and then rebuild. If you only have time for one of the two artifacts, write the record — a record without prose is still findable; prose without a record is not.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-001 calls lost traceability irreversible. Knowledge that exists but cannot be reached by the traversal the protocol mandates is, operationally, lost.
rules.evidence: Zagentexecution/quality_checks/incident_record_coverage_check.py; incidents.json 7 -> 10 records s099

rules.rule: A search that returns nothing is evidence about the SEARCH, not about the system. Before concluding 'X does not exist', prove the search could have found X: check the file ENCODING (UTF-16 returns 0 for every ASCII pattern), the CASE (ABAP source is conventionally lowercase; SAP field names are quoted uppercase in docs), and whether you searched the FULL body or a stub. Then check the ABSTRACTION: a table-level search cannot see logic that lives behind an exit call — GB931 holds CHECKID '=U917', never the field the FORM reads.
rules.why: s099. Claim 116 was published TIER_1 saying the PPC capture control did not exist, on the strength of 'zero matches for LZBKZ in YRGGBS00's 1,592-line source'. The file is UTF-16 and the ABAP is lowercase; FORM u917 sits at line 1547 and blocks the posting. Three silent failures stacked — wrong encoding, wrong case, and a corpus copy that was a 29-line stub. On that claim a KU was opened proposing four ways to BUILD a control that already existed, waiting on a decision from two named people. A zero-result search feels like evidence of absence and is the cheapest way to publish a confident lie.
rules.how_to_apply: Positive control first: grep for something you KNOW is in the file (its own FORM names, 'ENDFORM') and confirm you get hits. If that returns 0, your pipeline is broken, not the system. Use `python brain_v2/graph_queries.py code <obj>` to get the encoding-normalised primary source and the STUB_AT_CANONICAL flag before grepping, and `graph_queries.py section <routine>` / `blocking_code` instead of raw text search for behaviour. State the negative as 'not found by <method>', never as 'does not exist'.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 demands verifiable evidence. An empty result set is only evidence once the method is shown capable of producing a non-empty one.

rules.rule: Never SUM a document amount without grouping by its currency, and never label the result with a currency you did not convert into. REGUH-RWBTR, BSEG-DMBTR/WRBTR, FPAYP-* are all in the document or payment currency. If a total must span currencies, either group by WAERS and report the vector, or convert explicitly and say so.
rules.why: s099. I reported Egypt's Citi exposure as 'USD 3,285,100' from SUM(RWBTR) over rows that were mostly EGP. The largest entries were 360,600 and 200,000 EGP — about USD 7,200 and USD 4,000. That single number turned a routine country configuration into what I presented as an order-of-magnitude outlier, and it drove a wrong recommendation until JP challenged it. A cross-currency sum is not merely imprecise; it manufactures a finding that does not exist.
rules.how_to_apply: Any SELECT that sums an amount must carry its currency field in the GROUP BY, or the query is wrong. When comparing entities, prefer COUNTS or shares — they are currency-free. State the currency of every figure you report, and if it is a mix, say 'mixed currencies, not summable'.
rules.cp_derivation_method: CP-003 demands exact numbers with checkable provenance. An amount without its unit is not a number, and a sum across units is not a measurement.

claims.claim: AVC available is a fund/cover-group level metric, not an FR-line-level metric. All FR lines on the same (FONDS, FUNDSCTR, CMMTITEM-rolled-to-control-object) draw from a single shared AVC pool. The pool is calculated as: Available = FMAVCT.allotment - sum(open FMIOI commitments) - sum(FMIFIIT actuals) on the same key. FMAVC005 fires when Available <= 0 + new posting amount > 0. The triggering FR line is incidental; the constraint is the fund pool.

claims.claim: MULESOFT vs FB01 path distinction (user clarification Session #69): MULESOFT integration moves BOR (Budget Original Reservation, budget-side only) - it does NOT move commitments or real postings. FB01 is a real-posting RECLASSIFICATION transaction in FI - it moves actual money between accounts/funds in the live ledger. They serve different purposes: (1) MULESOFT = automated budget loading at biennium-start, carries Workplan/Allocation context including FIPEX-aware Commitment_Item__c. (2) FB01 = manual real-posting reclassifications (mid-biennium adjustments, biennium-end revenue moves like A_BANSAL 257-doc batch). Implication for fix paths: FIX-A (MULESOFT FIPEX-aware) ONLY helps biennium-start budget loading. It has NO effect on FB01 reclassifications, which produce the actual model-gap defect at biennium-end. The 257 FB01s on 2026-01-31 are real postings - they bypass any MULESOFT enhancement. Therefore: FIX-A scope is narrow. FIX-E (pre-flight HARD-BLOCK on FB01/FMBB/FMBBT) is necessary. FIX-F (Meta-AVC) is the ONLY path that catches every change source (budget OR real, automated OR manual).

claims.claim: META-AVC architecture (user proposal Session #69, FIX-F): Replace the two independent AVC engines (FM-AVC at Fund/FundCenter/CommItem granularity + PS-AVC at WBS granularity) with a SINGLE meta-AVC engine that holds the combined availability state and validates BOTH granularities atomically at posting time. The meta-AVC blocks a posting if (1) FM pool < 0 OR (2) PS pool < 0 OR (3) FM-pool and PS-pool DIVERGE (which is exactly the INC-005638 signature). claims.claim: Root config that PERMITS the FM-PS model gap (TIER_1 from fmavct_2026): UNESCO's AVC derivation rule FMAFMAP013500109 (env 9HZ00001) collapses 8 of the 9 operational FIPEX (11, 13, 20, 30, 40, 50, 10\' and REVENUE) into a SINGLE control object called TC. Only PSC (FIPEX 80) keeps its own separate control object. Therefore the AVC engine validates against only 2 buckets per fund (TC + 80) instead of the 9 FIPEX visible in FMIFIIT. The TC bucket includes REVENUE in its pool, so as long as REVENUE > sum(operational consumption), TC stays positive and AVC permits postings — even though individual operational FIPEX are deeply negative. AVC is structurally blind to per-FIPEX deficits because it never sees them. UNESCO-wide pattern: 6,550 control objects use TC aggregator out of ~9,500 FMAVCT_2026 rows = ~80% of fund-FundCenter combinations are vulnerable to this exact pattern. Two root-config fixes: FIX-G1 (modify FMAFMAP013500109 so each FIPEX has its own control object — granular AVC) or FIX-G2 (keep TC aggregation but exclude REVENUE from the pool). Either is ~1 sprint config + UAT — cheapest structural fix yet identified, alternative to FIX-E/F.

claims.claim: UNESCO custom ABAP class YCL_YPS8_BCS_BL contains hardcoded REVENUE placeholder preservation logic. Lines 58 and 73 of YCL_YPS8_BCS_BL===CM005_RPY.abap explicitly state: DELETE LT_WFMBDT WHERE HAMOUNT IS INITIAL AND FIPEX <> 'REVENUE'. This means: when processing budget data, zero-amount rows are removed EXCEPT for those on FIPEX=REVENUE. This is a custom-coded design choice that preserves the REVENUE bucket as the sole valid placeholder for unallocated budget. Combined with the MULESOFT integration that loads revenue exclusively to this FIPEX, it explains why operational FIPEX (11, 13, 20, 30, 40, 50, 80, 10) never receive direct revenue allocation. The actual MULESOFT flow is in MuleSoft GitLab/Artifactory (not in extracted_code repos). claims.claim: INC-000008088 Treasury interest GL split is constrained by an architectural invariant: bank statements can only be re-routed to specific GLs when the bank emits a SPECIFIC external transaction code (e.g. NINT — Normal Interest) that distinguishes interest from other credits. At UNESCO, only Societe Generale exposes NINT reliably; all other Treasury HQ banks (BNP-Paribas, CIC, CRCAM, Banque Populaire, Citibank, Standard Chartered, Northern Trust BFM/HED, etc.) use generic NTRF for interest credits. Therefore the final implementation of INC-8088 splits ONLY the SOG banks (Group A → 7044013 via existing INTEREST_REC mask redirect; Group B → 7044014 via NEW SOG_FRB + 111B + INTEREST_REC_B). Group C (ASHI/Nessim) and Group D (PFF) remain on 7044011 as a known limitation, accepted by Treasury (M. Spronk validated 2026-05-05). The original architectural plan (TR_TRNFA/B/C/D + SOG_FRA + 111A/B/C/D + INTEREST_REC_A/B/C/D — 4-way clone) is OBSOLETE.

claims.claim: WBS PS-budget channel is GUI-only (CJ30/KBPP family) — no clean single-call RFC equivalent. KBPP_EXTERN_UPDATE raises DA300 NOT_FOUND without the full CJ30 buffer/profile context even with IMP_CHECK=X. Custom Y*BUDGET* FMs are readers/loggers only; BAPI_BUS2054_SET_STATUS = status only; BAPI_0050_CREATE = FM fund-center object (OBJNR FS*), NOT WBS (OBJNR PR*). WBS budgeting is a TWO-STEP process: (1) CJ30 sets the original/current budget → stored in BPJA as WRTTP=41 (current budget); (2) CJ32 releases it → stored in BPJA as WRTTP=42 (released budget). Budget is ANNUAL (table BPJA by GJAHR), NOT overall (BPGE WRTTP=01 was empty for WBS 650RER0008 / OBJNR PR00021132). Corrects the earlier '0 budget in P01' which only checked BPGE/overall — BPJA WRTTP=41 (GJAHR=2026) had the 10,000 USD entry. BPGE WRTTP=01 = overall-level; BPJA WRTTP=41 = annual current; BPJA WRTTP=42 = annual released; VERSN=000 throughout. Budget-exceeded message = BP/604 (PS-AVC engine, not FM-AVC). RESOLVED s-2026-07-01 (was open — see KU-2026-CJ32-RELEASE-NOT-LANDING, now closed): PS-AVC/BP-604 checks the RELEASED budget WRTTP=42 (set by CJ32), NOT the original/current WRTTP=41 (set by CJ30). Proof: WBS 650RER0008 (OBJNR PR00021132) has WRTTP=41=10,000 USD for FY2026 but WRTTP=42=0, and BP/604 still fires on a posting attempt — the WRTTP=41 entry alone does not satisfy AVC. Therefore CJ32 release is MANDATORY, not just CJ30; the two-step CJ30→CJ32 sequence is a hard AVC precondition, not merely bookkeeping.

claims.claim: Structured-address scope clarification (resolves the project's core question, TIER_1): AdrLine (free-text address line) satisfies payment DELIVERY (the payment clears) but is NOT 'structured address' in the ISO 20022 / SWIFT CBPR+ / EPC sense (machine-parseable, separately tagged StrtNm/BldgNb/PstCd/TwnNm/CtrySubDvsn/Ctry). claims.claim: FMAVCT (AVC totals ledger 9H) rows on V01 exceed RFC_READ_TABLE's 512-byte line buffer -- the same field-split + row-index-merge technique used elsewhere in this landscape (rfc_helpers.rfc_read_paginated) is required: split the field list into <=8-field chunks, issue one ROWSKIPS-free (ROWCOUNT=0) call per chunk per year, then merge rows by index position. A per-year row-count-equality guard across chunks is mandatory (a mismatch means the index-merge is unsafe and the year must be skipped, not merged blindly). WHERE-clause equality options need spaces around '=' ("RYEAR = '2026'"); "RYEAR='2026'" (no spaces) raises OPTION_NOT_VALID/DB_Error on this wrapper. RRCTY discriminates budget (1, ~7.2k rows in 2024) vs consumption (0, ~6.9k rows in 2024); RCVRGRP_9 is uniformly blank on V01; RVERS='000', RLDNR='9H'. claims.claim: CONCRETE Nov-2026 CBPR+ structured-address rule (TIER_1, bank's own validation guide, quoted verbatim in the bank's test-tool result, 2026-07-02): "This guide applies November 2026 rules: when <PstlAdr> is provided, <TwnNm> & <Ctry> tags are mandatory. claims.claim: RFC_READ_TABLE reads of wide tables on P01 (such as FMAVCT with 77 fields / 38-col schema) require field-split batching: split columns into groups of <=7, RFC-read each group, recombine by row position with an equal-rowcount guard (assert all groups return the same number of rows). This is necessary because RFC_READ_TABLE has a 512-byte WA (work area) buffer and returns BUFFER_OVERFLOW beyond that limit. P01 also rejects ROWSKIPS (SAIS restriction -- claim #244); workaround = ROWCOUNT=0 partitioned by RFIKRS x RYEAR. Pattern implemented in scripts/extraction/psm_avc_refresh.py; reuse for any future wide-table RFC extraction from P01.
claims.resolution_notes: Reusable tooling pattern. The 512-byte WA buffer is a known RFC_READ_TABLE constraint; this documents the working workaround tested against P01 FMAVCT. Cross-link: claim #244 (P01 SAIS ROWSKIPS rejection). Script: scripts/extraction/psm_avc_refresh.py.

evidence_for.cite: Field-split implementation: FMAVCT 77 fields split into <=7-col groups; each RFC-read; recombined by position; guard: assert all groups same row count. ROWCOUNT=0 per RFIKRS x RYEAR avoids ROWSKIPS. Tested live P01: 18,838 rows FY2024 / 16,112 FY2025 / 13,593 FY2026 -- all cross-split counts match.

claims.claim: The AVC control key is 4-PART: Fund Area (RFIKRS) + Fund (RFUND) + Fund Center (RFUNDSCTR) + Commitment Item (RCMMTITEM), per fiscal year (RYEAR), ledger 9H, version, and record type RRCTY (budget vs actual). Fund Area is MANDATORY, not optional: Fund Center and Commitment Item codes (TC, 11, 13, VNI, HEQ, NAI, ...) are area-scoped and repeat across the 9 FM areas (UNES 11,390 rows, ICTP 741, IIEP 559, UBO 377, MGIE 171, UIS 108, UIL 89, ICBA 89, IBE 69 in fmavct_2026), so any AVC read/group-by/join keyed on (Fund, FundCenter, CmmtItem) WITHOUT RFIKRS collides control objects across institutes. Gold DB fmavct_2024/2025/2026 carry all four dims as explicit columns (RFIKRS/RFUND/RFUNDSCTR/RCMMTITEM); always include RFIKRS in the query key.

claims.claim: THREE LAYERS, NOT ONE (s097). Keying domains on SAP modules (FI, CO, MM, SD) conflates a TECHNICAL taxonomy with a business one: nobody in an organisation does 'FI', they pay an invoice or commit a budget, and every such act crosses several modules. Worse, `_module_to_domain` was ONE-TO-ONE and cannot be — FI-BL-PT pays suppliers (P2P), staff (payroll), travellers and treasury deals; PSM-FM serves B2C2A, P2P commitment checking, POST2BUDGET and PROJ2FUND. The model now separates COMPONENT (SAP's taxonomy, deterministic, not ours to rename) / DOMAIN (who owns it) / FLOW (what the organisation does end to end), with MANY-TO-MANY edges between all three. claims.claim: REGUH and FMIOI — classified, catalogued, and three traps recorded that produce confident wrong numbers. REGUH (3,707,737 rows, LAUFD 20160104–20260512) is the PAYMENT-RUN HEADER and serves BOTH Payment_BCM and FI-AP: it is where an AP open item becomes a disbursement, so an AP analysis that skips it stops at the invoice. TRAP 1 — a PROPOSAL is not a PAYMENT: XVORL='X' on 358,106 rows (9.7%) are F110 proposal runs; counting REGUH rows as payments overstates by that much and every row looks identical. TRAP 2 — KUNNR is part of the SAP key (LAUFD+LAUFI+ZBUKR+LIFNR+KUNNR+EMPFG+VBLNR) and was NOT extracted; 1,748 key collisions are the direct consequence. TRAP 3 — PERNR is populated on 1,195,826 rows (32%): those are payments to EMPLOYEES, making REGUH an HCM-Payment bridge rather than a pure AP table, so any 'vendor payment' metric over the whole table is wrong by a third. FMIOI (2,190,893 rows, GJAHR 2017–2026, 8,380 funds, 9 company codes) is the FM COMMITMENT line-item table — the commitment leg of budget->commitment->actual (flow B2C2A). REFBT names the committing document: 110 funds reservation 1,381,250 · 020 purchase order 588,255 · 040 purchase requisition 172,517 · 010 42,746 · 060 6,125. Its registry row count was STALE by 376,950 (1,813,943 declared vs 2,190,893 actual). TRAP 4 — the WRTTP distribution invites an available = budget - commitment - actual formula; that is REFUTED ([[feedback_avc_real_from_standard_not_handrolled]]). FMIOI answers what is COMMITTED and against which document, never what is LEFT.

claims.claim: ALGORITHM A8 — CHANGE-TO-EXECUTOR ATTRIBUTION, the generic enrichment. Built s097 by generalising the PBC analysis on the spot: joining a STATE-CHANGE stream to an EXECUTION stream on (user, day, hour) answers WHAT WRITES a thing for ANY domain, and the same shape answers which program sends an IDoc type, which job produces a file, which process touches an interface. THREE SCORINGS WERE WRONG BEFORE ONE WAS RIGHT, and this is the durable content. (1) RAW COINCIDENCE named a spool artifact `!QGYAO==========A_SEFI0410` as the writer of FMRESERV, because the RFC dispatcher runs constantly and coincides with everything. (2) LIFT removed that and INVERTED the error: it rewards rarity, so it ranked HUNCALC0 — the actual PBC engine — below noise and filtered it out at a 1.5 threshold. HUNCALC0 runs on 91 of 108 days, base rate 0.84, so its lift cannot exceed 1.19 however perfect the coincidence. AN ENGINE IS NOT RARE: running whenever the class changes is precisely what makes it the engine. (3) SMALL DENOMINATORS: a program that ran ONE day of 108 scored lift 27 on a single coincidence — the same defect as D6's z-score over a two-month baseline in different clothes. THE SCORE IS THE PHI COEFFICIENT over the 2x2 contingency table of (day,hour) slots: symmetric, correcting for both base rates, and a program present in every slot has d=0 so its margin collapses and it scores nothing. TWO CONSTRAINTS the user specified and that make it correct: TIME not day (2,493 hour slots vs 108 days — programs in the same nightly chain separate), and EXCLUSIVITY (a program claimed by >=5 classes is AMBIGUOUS; attributing one writer to every table is the failure the constraint prevents). CHANNEL CLASSIFICATION, from the user's second point: an EMPTY TCODE is not 'batch', it usually means a BAPI or RFC whose interface design never set one. So a dispatcher ranking high is EVIDENCE OF AN INTERFACE CHANNEL rather than noise to filter, and the calling function modules are named from PARAM3 — which is the hand-off into F1 (interface boundary) and F2 (satellites). Classes are labelled DIALOG / PROGRAM / INTERFACE. CONTROL RESULT: the algorithm independently recovers known-correct writers — RM_MEPO_GUI for EINKBELEG (purchase orders), RM_MEREQ_GUI for BANF (requisitions), the HR engine chain RHHCP_DC_EMPLOYEE / RHRFPM_ENGINE_PA30 for PBC and FMRESERV — while demoting SAPMSSY1 to AMBIGUOUS everywhere. 72 object classes, 3,280 programs, 2,493 slots.

claims.claim: THE PBC ENCUMBRANCE RULES, READ FROM PRODUCTION — the AS-DESIGNED half of the largest write path in the installation (s097). Five decisions, each confirmed line by line in ZCL_IM__UNESCO_ENCUMB (1,296 lines, P01): R1 A POST COMMITS ONLY WHILE VACANT. DO_HANDLE_VACANCY drops any position whose HROBJECT_DP is populated (occupied) and clears the position pointer on the person — so an occupied post commits nothing of its own and the commitment comes from the PERSON. That is what prevents post and holder being counted twice. The code carries its own statement of intent: 'UNESCO requires Precommitment ONLY for vacant and integrated positions'. CAVEAT: the comment says the pointer deletion is 'deactivated' while the code does it — comment and code disagree, code is authoritative. R2 COMMITMENTS PRO-RATE BY DATE INTERSECTION. Three cases in ADJUST_REQ_WITH_VALIDITY: no overlap skipped, containment kept whole, partial overlap SPLIT with the amount re-derived by ADJUST_COST_DIST_AMOUNT. Never all-or-nothing at a period boundary. R3 THE BIENNIUM — this CLOSES the gap claim #358 recorded as unknown. DET_BIENNIUM_FROM_ENC_IV asserts the encumbrance interval must end 31 December and span at least one year, then sets biennium.BEGDA = interval.BEGDA and biennium.ENDDA(4) = BEGDA(4) + 1. claims.claim: THERE IS NO VACANCY TOLERANCE — THE AUTHORED RULE P2B-3 DESCRIBES AN INTENT THE SYSTEM DOES NOT IMPLEMENT (s097, read from production source). P2B-3 states that 'a vacant post does not hold a commitment beyond its declared vacancy tolerance'. Read in P01: ZCL_IM__UNESCO_ENCUMB_VACANCY~DO_REQUIREMENT_FILTRATION delegates straight to DO_HANDLE_VACANCY, which only calls SUPER — so the vacancy filter is BINARY, vacant or not, with no duration term anywhere. Its DO_HANDLE_COMMITMENT_PERIOD is literally `ASSERT 1 = 2.` with the comment 'No filtering over period ==> in this scenario this is done in ZCL_IM__UNESCO_ENCUMB_ENCPER' — a deliberate guard saying this path must never execute. And ENCPER's IF_HRFPM_DC_PERIOD~OBJECT_GET_PERIOD does not bound the vacancy either: it takes the encumbrance validity interval and CUTS IT WITH THE OBJECT'S OWN EXISTENCE INTERVAL. SO A VACANT POST HOLDS ITS COMMITMENT FOR THE WHOLE FUNDING WINDOW, however long it has been vacant. Three things bound the commitment and NONE of them is a tolerance: the encumbrance interval/biennium (PBC-R3), the object's existence interval (this method), and the extension horizon MV_EXTENSION_YEARS (PBC-R4). All three are windows of the FUNDING or of the OBJECT; none limits how long a vacancy may lock budget. This is the answer to the question the reconciliation left open, and it is the second of the two possibilities: not 'the tolerance lives elsewhere' but 'the authored rule states an intent that is not implemented'. Whether it SHOULD be is a decision for the budget office, not a defect to fix silently.

claims.claim: THE ATTRIBUTION FINDING IS ALSO A LICENSING FINDING, AND IT IS THE FIRST CONCRETE CONTENT FOR R_S4_READINESS (s097, user insight). The same measurement that shows 5.3M calls with no attributable actor also describes the tenant's DIGITAL ACCESS exposure, because SAP licenses indirect use by DOCUMENTS CREATED THROUGH NON-DIALOG CHANNELS — which is precisely what algorithm A8 already derives per object class. THE STRUCTURE OF THE RISK. Today, a satellite calling over RFC under a technical account costs a system-user licence and nothing per call. On S/4HANA — and far more sharply on S/4HANA CLOUD — that same traffic is API consumption and Digital Access documents. This tenant's operating model is 80% external, so the exposure is not a detail of the migration: it is the shape of the migration. Every integration that is free today becomes a metered cost. FMRESERV alone carries 6,951,908 change documents; the named writers already include BAPI_PO_CREATE1, BAPI_PR_CREATE, BAPI_INCOMINGINVOICE_CREATE1, BAPI_GOODSMVT_CREATE and ZBAPI_VENDOR_CREATE2 — all document-creating calls from outside. MULESOFT (3.23M calls, one identity), BRIDGE-RFC (2.11M, no caller field) and UBO-RFC (324K) cannot be attributed to a person — so they can be neither excused as named-user activity nor apportioned to a business owner. In a licensing negotiation, traffic you cannot attribute is traffic you cannot defend. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE MODEL: R_S4_READINESS was the ONE completely empty column across all 21 domains. It now has its first anchor, and the anchor is commercial rather than technical — which is probably why it stayed empty: we were looking for technical readiness factors.

What is genuinely theirs is the design corpus (33 sources / 46 original files) and the Salesforce side. SEVEN RANKED FILLERS, recorded as records in brain_v2/s_standard_ref_sources.json. The distinction that decides their value: only the UMOJA (UN Secretariat, 199pp) and OECD fit-gap material is genuinely SAP-STANDARD; the BBPs are UNESCO's AS-DESIGNED intent authored by SAP SE / SAP Suisse / Capgemini. THE HEADLINE, and it is the largest conformance finding this project has produced: BBP-04 defines FM AREA CONSOLIDATION — nine areas into one, `UNSC` — and calls it a HARD PREREQUISITE on which consolidated reporting, a unified commitment-item catalog and a single derivation strategy all depend. PRODUCTION RUNS NINE FM AREAS: IBE, ICBA, ICTP, IIEP, MGIE, UBO, UIL, UIS, UNES — measured in fmioi.BUKRS and fmavct_2026.RFIKRS, and it is the 2017 AS-IS list itself minus IESALC and IITE. Nine years on, the structure the design was written to replace is still the structure. This is not a pending item: a unified catalog and a single strategy are not partially achievable across nine areas, so a large part of BBP-04 is UNREACHABLE rather than unfinished. FIVE RULES INGESTED with the delta attached to each. S1 single FM area NOT_IMPLEMENTED. S2 the seven BCS dimensions PARTIAL, because dimension 3 (Grant) requires GM and GM has ZERO tables in the golden — and because our own bridge still carries PROJ.PSPID = GEBER as a static proxy, i.e. project-as-fund, the exact equivalence the design set out to reverse. S3 the AVC ADDRESS TRIPLE (Posting / Budget / Control) CONFORMS — the control record is keyed Fund x Fund Center x GROUPED commitment item, matching the design's own worked example. S4 FMDERIVE DEVIATES: the outcome holds but the mechanism is the user exit ZXFMDTU02_RPY rather than a table-driven strategy, so the user experience conforms and the maintainability does not. S5 PBET UNVERIFIED. THE MOST USEFUL RULE IS THE ONE THAT CONFORMS. S3 gives us the VOCABULARY our own avc_availability_model.md lacked: we had measured the control address correctly and had no name for the distinction between posting, budget and control addresses. It also explains WHY the hand-rolled `available = budget - commitment - actual` was refuted — that formula assumes posting address equals control address, and here it does not. A standard reference earns its keep by naming what you already measured. PSM_FM S_STANDARD_REF NONE -> PARTIAL and G_CONFORMANCE NONE -> PARTIAL. PARTIAL and not HAVE on purpose: one document of seven, one domain of six.

claims.claim: THE SEVEN-DIMENSIONAL BCS RUNS AS THREE DIMENSIONS (s097, measured against the SAP-standard coding block from the UN Secretariat's Umoja reference). Across 2,308,814 FM line items in fmifiit_full: Fund (FONDS) 100%, Funds Center (FISTL) 100%, Commitment Item (FIPEX) 100% — and then four empty. Funded Program (MEASURE) 0.0%. Functional Area (FAREA) 0.0%, its only distinct value being blank. Grant 0%, consistent with GM having zero tables. Budget Period column absent entirely. THIS IS NOT A SHORTFALL AT THE MARGIN: four of seven dimensions carry no value in a single row out of 2.3 million. FUNCTIONAL AREA IS THE ONE THAT SHOULD ALARM. BBP-04 defines it as UNESCO's C/5 EXPECTED RESULTS — the programme structure, used for STATUTORY REPORTING BY PROGRAMME OBJECTIVE. It is the dimension that ties money to purpose, and it is blank in every row, which means budget consumption cannot be reported by programme objective from FM at all. For an organisation whose mandate is literally expressed as C/5 Expected Results, that is the gap worth taking to the business. FUNDED PROGRAM BEING EMPTY EXPLAINS SOMETHING BOTH PROJECTS HAD ONLY OBSERVED. It is the designed WBS-to-FM bridge. Our model and theirs both carry PROJ.PSPID = GEBER — project-as-fund — and both label it a STATIC PROXY without explaining why it survives. It survives because the designed bridge dimension carries nothing: the fund code is the only project link that exists. Two open questions turn out to be one answered fact. METHOD NOTE: this is the first measurement in the project made against a genuinely SAP-STANDARD yardstick rather than against UNESCO's own design intent. BBP-04 says what UNESCO intended; the Umoja coding block says what SAP expects a public-sector posting to carry. Measuring against the second is a different and stronger claim, and it is why the peer material was ranked first among the S_STANDARD_REF sources.

claims.claim: THE BUDGET RATE MECHANISM WAS DESIGNED AWAY AND BUILT ANYWAY — and its failure mode is the reason it was designed away (s097, BBP-08 against production). BBP-08 calls it 'the most significant simplification': the practice of a special CONSTANT EXCHANGE RATE for EUR-to-USD conversion IN BUDGET EXECUTION is ELIMINATED. Constant dollar becomes strictly a REPORTING concept, an extra BW column. Budget control instead uses an additional AVC in BCS with a tolerance (~105%) RATHER THAN MANIPULATING POSTING EXCHANGE RATES — expressly so that postings use operational rates, for IPSAS. WHAT EXISTS IN PRODUCTION IS THE OPPOSITE: YCL_FM_BR_EXCHANGE_RATE_BL manipulates the exchange rate during budget execution. And it carries a one-line defect confirmed in source — the conversion gate appends only 'EUR' to mr_waers, so a USD posting exits via CHECK without setting rv_is_ok and the conversion is SKIPPED SILENTLY. A trace recorded 42 invocations of the class and ZERO reads of TCURR: it fired and converted nothing. MEASURED BLAST RADIUS, already established in INC-BUDGETRATE-EQG and now attached to the rule: 458 funds carry EUR-loaded reservations with USD consumption; 135,792 bypass postings lifetime; $375,011,484.95 of volume; ~$35.7M of theoretical AVC drift exposure; 70 funds still exposed in 2026 with 214 bypass postings already made. WHY THIS IS THE CLEAREST DEMONSTRATION IN THE PROJECT OF WHY S_STANDARD_REF MATTERS: without the as-designed reference the incident reads as 'a bug to fix'. With it, the same facts read as 'a mechanism the blueprint explicitly eliminated was implemented, and the failure it produces is the very reason for the elimination'. The design's alternative — an AVC tolerance in BCS — cannot have this failure class at all, because it never touches the posting rate. Same evidence, different conclusion, and a different remedy: fix the gate, or retire the mechanism for what BBP-08 specified. AND AN IPSAS ANGLE THAT IS NOT OURS TO DECIDE: the design's stated reason for the deletion was that postings must use OPERATIONAL exchange rates. A mechanism that overrides the posting rate is therefore not merely fragile — it sits against the standard the design was aligning to. That is a question for the business.

claims.claim: THE BUDGET RATE SOLUTION READ FROM PRODUCTION — the perimeter, the three gates and a SECOND latent defect of the same shape as the known one (s097, package YA extracted from P01: 136 objects; 18 in the BR family — 5 classes, 1 composite ENHC, 12 ENHO). FIRST, AN EVIDENCE CORRECTION: the incident cited extracted_code/CLAS/YCL_FM_BR_EXCHANGE_RATE_BL/CM00A as the source of the one-line defect, and THAT PATH DOES NOT EXIST in any of the three corpora. The root cause was confirmed by a debugger session and a trace, which is strong evidence — but the most-quoted line was unreadable until now. The real source is extracted_sap_p01/YA/YCL_FM_BR_EXCHANGE_RATE_BL.abap, 634 lines. THE APPLICABILITY PERIMETER IS EIGHT DIMENSIONS, all of which must pass, each a CHECK that exits silently: ledger = 9A (note: NOT the AVC ledger 9H); company code = UNES; FM area = UNES; business area = GEF; currency = EUR ONLY (the defect); commitment item EXCLUDES GAINS and REVENUE; transaction EXCLUDES HRM1/HRM2/HRP1, so PBC pre-commitment, PBC commitment and payroll are OUT of the main path; and fund type IN a DATA-DRIVEN set from FMFUNDTYPE WHERE ZZFIX_RATE = X — measured in P01 as 14 types, all UNES (001-005, 009, 010, 012, 013, 016-018, 094, 095), i.e. Regular Programme only. Earmarked 101-115, MBF 299 and CRP 311/314 are NOT in the perimeter. THERE IS AN ACTIVATION SWITCH NOBODY HAD RECORDED: CHECK_BR_IS_ACTIVE compares sy-datum against MV_START_DATE, read from the TVARVC variable Y_FM_FIXED_RATE_START. Measured in P01: 20240101, so BR has been active since 1 January 2024. THE TRAP: if that variable is missing, the code defaults the date to '99991231' and BR silently never activates — a kill switch that fails closed and says nothing. THREE GATES, NOT ONE, and the difference between them is where the asymmetry lives. CHECK_CONDITIONS is the main path: EUR only, PBC and payroll excluded. CHECK_CONDITIONS_2 is the STAFF path: it accepts EUR *and* USD and INCLUDES HRM1/HRM2/HRP1 — so the cure for the currency defect exists inside the class and is unreachable from the main path. CHECK_CONDITIONS_3 is the complement, used for DELETION during RFFMREPO reconstruction: inverted membership on ledger/company/FM-area/business-area, and it INCLUDES what the others exclude. A SECOND LATENT DEFECT, NEW: the staff gate also checks IV_HKONT IN MR_HKONT, and MR_HKONT is DECLARED at line 57 and NEVER POPULATED anywhere in the class. In ABAP a value IN an empty range is FALSE, so whenever a GL account is passed the staff gate FAILS ALWAYS. Same shape as the known mr_waers defect — a range that gates and is never filled — and it means the one path that would have handled USD is itself closed on that condition.

claims.claim: THE BUDGET-RATE SOLUTION HAS TWO FUND PERIMETERS AND THEY DISAGREE (s097, read from P01 production source). EXECUTION side, YCL_FM_BR_EXCHANGE_RATE_BL: the fund-type range is built from FMFUNDTYPE WHERE ZZFIX_RATE = X — data-driven, measured as 14 types in UNES (001-005, 009, 010, 012, 013, 016-018, 094, 095). REPORTING side, YFM_CONSTANT_DOLLAR plus its variants _V2 and _DB_V2: S_TYPE is DEFAULTED at INITIALIZATION to a LITERAL range 001 to 099, commented 'Set fund type for GEF'. THE 14 FLAGGED TYPES ALL SIT INSIDE 001-099, BUT THE RANGE IS FAR WIDER. So a fund whose type falls in 001-099 without the ZZFIX_RATE flag appears in the constant-dollar report having NEVER been converted at execution. The report and the engine do not agree on who is in scope, and nothing reconciles them — which is the shape that produces 'the report says one thing and the system did another'. A NUANCE THAT CHANGES HOW TO FIX IT: S_TYPE is a SELECT-OPTIONS defaulted at INITIALIZATION, not a hard gate. An operator can widen or narrow it on the selection screen, so the reporting perimeter is whatever is left on the screen — and the mismatch with execution is silent in both directions. AND THE HARD-CODED LIST IS STILL THERE, COMMENTED: lines 92 and 97 of the class carry 'APPEND ... low = 019' behind a quote, the predecessor of the select. Two generations of perimeter logic sitting in one constructor.

claims.claim: THE BLUEPRINT'S AS-IS IS THE SYSTEM'S AS-RUN, NINE YEARS ON — three measurements converge (s097, BBP-06 ingested for Cost_Recovery_CRP). BBP-06 is described in the programme as its most comprehensive blueprint, because extra-budgetary donor funding is a major part of UNESCO's activity. It designs SAP Grants Management as a FIRST-CLASS MODULE: five dimensions (Grant, Fund, Sponsored Class, Sponsored Program, validity), a seven-stage lifecycle with status-driven workflow, GM as a BUDGETARY SUB-LEDGER to FM-BCS, multi-funding for EU agreements, and EUR grant handling for UIL and ICTP. ZERO gm* TABLES EXIST. None of it was built. THE SHARPER FINDING IS IN ITS DESCRIPTION OF THE PROBLEM. BBP-06 states the AS-IS it set out to replace: donor agreements tracked OUTSIDE SAP in SPREADSHEETS and SISTER, 'with only indirect representation through MISUSED FUND AND WBS MASTER DATA OBJECTS'. Every element of that sentence is measurable today. GM: zero tables. The misused FUND object: PROJ.PSPID = GEBER, project-as-fund, still the only project link and labelled a static proxy by both this project and the peer one. The misused WBS object: Funded Program, the designed WBS-to-FM bridge, populated in 0.0% of 2,308,814 FM line items. THREE INDEPENDENT THREADS MEET HERE. BBP-04 insisted Fund means the FUNDING SOURCE and explicitly NOT the project, calling the reversal a design principle. BBP-06 named the misuse of Fund and WBS as the problem. The data shows the misuse intact and the replacement dimension empty. So on this axis the blueprint's AS-IS is the system's AS-RUN — which is not a gap in the model but the finding the model exists to produce. ALSO INGESTED: revenue recognition is designed as DEFERRED at invoice and RECOGNISED at cash receipt — an IPSAS policy, not a technical detail. Marked UNVERIFIED: without GM the designed mechanism cannot exist, and whether an equivalent deferral runs in FI has not been checked. If it does not, the accounting answer is either produced some other way or not produced. Cost_Recovery_CRP S_STANDARD_REF NONE -> PARTIAL.

claims.claim: THE B2R YARDSTICK IS THE AS-RUN, NOT THE BLUEPRINT — frame correction on my own ingest (s097, user-directed). WHAT I DID WRONG: I read the 2017 BBPs and measured production against them, producing 17 rules whose verdicts were mostly NOT_IMPLEMENTED. The MEASUREMENTS are real and stand — nine FM areas, zero gm* tables, 18 commitment items, Functional Area and Funded Program blank across 2,308,814 rows. THE FRAME WAS WRONG. Measuring against a superseded design turns 'the organisation built something else' into 'the system failed', and those are different claims with different remedies. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, measured from both ends independently: UNESCO kept SAP as the SYSTEM OF RECORD and moved the SYSTEM OF ENGAGEMENT entirely outside it — Salesforce / Core Planner, ORION, named-user portals. Not around SAP; IN FRONT OF it. The peer project derived this from the Salesforce event log (23,730 status events, 26,075 posting events); we derived the same model from the SAP audit log (15.6M RFC calls). Two instruments, one model. THE REAL B2R END-TO-END, measured per workplan on real timestamps: plan to Validated median 20.9 DAYS (p90 428) — the human planning loop; Validated to first SAP posting median 1.8 DAYS — the integration seam; 5,929 workplans reached SAP and 91.7% carry a Financial_Summary return; 26,075 posting events of which 82.9% are budget transfers. SO THE BOTTLENECK IS HUMAN VALIDATION, NOT TECHNOLOGY AND NOT CONFIGURATION. The cross-system handoff is near-instant. Any B2R improvement effort aimed at SAP configuration is aimed at the fast part. THE FAILURE MODES ARE NAMED AND ATTRIBUTED: the forward sync is SERIAL and STOP-ON-FIRST-ERROR, so one failing object halts an entire workplan. 103 workplans and 354 allocations carry errors — fund create/assign ~130 (top single error: 'Assignment to 43 C/5 not possible with fund validity 01.01.2024-31.12.2025', 39 times), project create ~67. And INT-05, the Fund Center master channel SAP to Core Planner, has been BLOCKED SINCE 2023. THE WARNING WAS ALREADY WRITTEN IN THEIR OWN WORK. knowledge/36 re-scored one of its own claims with this exact diagnosis — the 'manual entry' reading of FC/CC/FA was 'a DESIGN-DOC ARTIFACT OVERTAKEN BY THE AS-RUN' — and deprecates any dialog-based baseline outright: 'a redesign baselined on dialog usage is baselined on <20% of the real traffic'. I walked into the failure mode their document names. WHAT THE BBP INGEST IS STILL WORTH: archaeology and vocabulary. The AVC address triple named a distinction we had measured and could not name, and that keeps its value. The rest is a record of what was intended, not a scorecard for what is.

claims.claim: THE MODEL DIMENSIONS LIVE IN THE IDENTIFIER STRING, NOT IN THE SCHEMA — measured end-to-end on the golden (s098, ALGORITHM A10). THE FM LEDGER POSTS ON EXACTLY TWO LEGS. In fmifiit_full, 2,308,814 actual lines: FONDS 100%, FISTL 100%, FIPEX 100% — and MEASURE (Funded Program), FAREA (Functional Area), GRANT_NBR and PRCTR are populated in 0.0%. MEASURE is the DESIGNED WBS-to-FM bridge, so the designed chain from work to money does not exist in the data. AND THERE IS NO FOREIGN KEY EITHER. prps carries no fund and no fund-centre column; proj carries none. Nothing in the PS master points at FM. YET THE CHAIN RESOLVES AT 99.5%, THROUGH THE STRING. Every WBS identifier is <fund code>.<level>.<level>: taking the root before the first dot, 59,424 of 59,749 WBS elements land on a real fund. The project id IS a fund code — 13,812 of 13,976 PSPID values (98.8%), the project-as-fund inversion the 2017 design explicitly forbade, still load-bearing. The 4-level spine is dot DEPTH, not a parent key. THE GRAMMAR IS ALSO A CLASSIFICATION. Three code families coexist in funds.FINCODE and each predicts the TYPE family: all-numeric 8 or 10 digits (73.2% of the UNES master) for RP/staff types 0xx; NNN+GEO+NNNN (20.8%) for extrabudgetary delivery types 1xx; alpha-prefixed legacy variants for older VC types. claims.claim: FUND RESERVATIONS ARE LONG-LIVED AND REPEATEDLY ADJUSTED, ON A BIENNIUM RHYTHM — NOT A MONTHLY ONE (s098, measured on 6,415,467 FMRESERV change headers). THE OPERATOR'S RECOLLECTION was that reservations are adjusted MONTH BY MONTH so the funds are never released. The data confirms the RETENTION and refutes the MONTHLY. WHAT IS MEASURED: 874,143 distinct reservation documents carry 6,415,467 changes, 7.3 per document on average — and FMRESERV is the largest change-document class in the system. Among documents that live SIX MONTHS OR MORE (416,680 of them), the median document is touched in 32% of the months it exists, with a median of 6 changes, and only 12% are touched in 80% or more of their months. So they are maintained repeatedly across a long life, not topped up every month. THE LIFETIME DISTRIBUTION IS THE REAL SIGNAL, and it is not smooth. It spikes hard at structural boundaries: 145,354 documents live exactly 13 months and 87,353 live exactly 25 months. Twenty-five months is a BIENNIUM. These reservations are created and carried to the end of a budget period rather than consumed and closed — which is the retention behaviour the recollection describes, running on the budget calendar instead of the monthly one. The 25-month cohort also carries the highest adjustment count, a median of 11 changes each. THE ARTIFACT THAT NEARLY PRODUCED A WRONG ANSWER, recorded because it is the more useful lesson: measured over ALL documents the ratio of months-with-a-change to months-of-life has a MEDIAN OF 0.96, which reads as 'touched in essentially every month of its life' and would have confirmed the monthly reading outright. It is an artifact. A document created and closed inside one month scores 1.00 by construction, and 34.7% of documents live exactly one month. Excluding short lives moves the median from 0.96 to 0.32. THE RATIO WAS MEASURING DOCUMENT LIFETIME, NOT ADJUSTMENT BEHAVIOUR. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: whether the AMOUNT moves down in step with consumption (a genuine commitment drawdown) or is restored (a hold). That needs the value history in CDPOS, which is deliberately deferred, or the amounts in fmioi joined per document.

claims.claim: FUNDED PROGRAM IS EMPTY BECAUSE THE DERIVATION THAT WOULD FILL IT WAS NEVER CONFIGURED — the causal chain, closed with evidence from P01 (s098). Those are different findings with different remedies, and until now we could not tell them apart. FOUR MEASUREMENTS, IN ORDER. (1) SAP's own rule: Funded Program is never assigned directly — in integrated postings its account assignment is ALWAYS DERIVED at posting time, via FMDERIVE, and it is BCS-only. (2) The derivation tool holds NO STRATEGY: T811C, T811S and T811K are EMPTY in P01, verified with and without a TAB='FMDERIVE' filter, returning zero rows rather than an error. (3) FMDERIVE IS NOT EVEN A REGISTERED DERIVATION POINT: T811X registers exactly four — CCSS, CEST7, GLPCT, JBDST7 — and FMDERIVE is not among them. (4) MEANWHILE THE MECHANISM ACTUALLY IN USE IS THE CLASSIC ONE AND IT IS FULLY POPULATED: TABADRSF carries 3,627 derivation rule rows, with TABADRST 253, TABADRS 170, TABADRX 43, TABADRH 32 and TABADRPCONF 20. THE CONCLUSION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ACCIDENTAL. UNESCO derives FM account assignments through the CLASSIC account-assignment derivation, which fills Fund, Fund Center and Commitment Item — exactly the three that measure 100% — and which CANNOT derive Funded Program. The mechanism that can derive it, the derivation tool behind FMDERIVE, was never configured at all. So the empty column is not neglect and not a switch that someone turned off: the organisation runs a derivation architecture in which that dimension has no way to be filled. WHY IT MATTERS FOR WHAT COMES NEXT: every proposal to 'start using Funded Program' is really a proposal to stand up a second derivation mechanism and migrate onto it, which is a different size of change from configuring a field. And it explains why the identifier convention exists — the grammar is not a shortcut around a working feature, it is the only carrier available under the architecture actually in place.

claims.claim: THE BUDGET-RATE PERIMETER IS EIGHT CONDITIONS AND EACH ONE IS SKIPPED WHEN THE CALLER PASSES IT EMPTY — so it is not a filter (s098, user direction: the conditions are in the classes, it is fund type AND currency AND more, and it is very specific).
